A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SaFa research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original audio and panorama generation experiments, ablations, and user-study results, including Tables 2–7 and Figures 9–10.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds a waveform-latent generation comparison in Appendix Section 8.2, Table 8.

M1.justification: The Self-Loop and Reference-Guided Latent Swap procedures, Algorithm 1, and default swap settings are retained. The Make2-specific SaFa+ adjustments already appear in v2; the added SD-audio evaluation does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same soundscape, sound-effect, music, and panorama tasks and retain AudioCaps and the existing prompts. The new waveform-latent experiment uses AudioCaps with another model configuration within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain their baseline membership. New Table 8 uses already evaluated methods—MD, MAD, and SD-audio—in the waveform configuration. SyncTweedies and StochSync are newly cited but are not evaluated.

E3.justification: V3 adds a 24-second generation evaluation using SD-audio waveform latents, restricting initial latent maps to 10 seconds and reporting FAD, FD, KL, and mCLAP on AudioCaps. The previously reported experimental and user-study protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, guidance-rate and swap-interval analyses, length-adaptation tests, and Make2 failure analysis are retained. Table 8 adds a backbone comparison rather than a new ablation, sensitivity sweep, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Empirical tables and user-preference plots retain point-estimate reporting. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests; the added table follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports SaFa results of FAD 4.19, FD 24.40, KL 1.96, and mCLAP 0.41, best among its four reported methods. These are additional waveform-setting results, not improvements over corresponding v2 scores. Tables 1–6, the panorama-length table (v2 Table 7; v3 Table 9), and existing qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical constructions and appendix proposition, assumptions, proof, and corollary are retained. Equation 8 corrects the averaging-mask label from Wswap to Wavg without changing the operation; the revised filter analogy is interpretive prose.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the core claims of a modality-agnostic two-swap framework, superior audio generation, and comparable panorama generation with a 2–20× speedup. V3 shortens the abstract's length-adaptation and generalizability wording, while retaining those claims elsewhere.

C2.justification: V2 describes averaging as an all-pass filter and swapping as a band-pass filter; v3 replaces this with an adaptive-filter analogy based on trajectory differences and describes aliasing reduction more cautiously. Appendix Section 8.2 also discusses waveform applicability and acknowledges the new experiment's unoptimized initialization.

D1.justification: V3 documents the open-source SD-audio checkpoint and 10-second initial latent-map restriction for the added experiment. Existing sampler settings, hardware information, Make2-specific implementation adjustments, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SyncTweedies and StochSync, describing their extension of synchronized diffusion to 3D mesh texturing. The remaining research positioning is retained; other reference changes largely concern numbering and bibliographic presentation.

P1.justification: V3 copyedits the abstract and main text, changes 'forward-only' to 'feed-forward,' and promotes the former methodology subsections into Sections 3–5. The narrative order remains largely unchanged, although some edits introduce awkward wording.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 8, resizes Figures 6 and 8, and expands Figure 2's caption to identify its axes. Existing illustrations are retained, with local layout reflow, updated cross-reference styling, and renumbering of the panorama-length table.

improvement.justification: The added waveform-latent comparison supplies useful evidence for applicability beyond spectrum latents, while the corrected mask notation and more careful filter explanation improve clarity. These gains are limited by the acknowledged unoptimized setup and minor editorial regressions, including a garbled introduction sentence and skipped Table 7 numbering. The central experiments and theoretical support remain unchanged.
